pr_title: Allow choosing a blank issue/pr template
pr_comments: In testing this I noticed our bug fix template has no name (not an issue when we weren't previously displaying it in a select menu); I pushed a commit to give it a name.

> In testing this I noticed our bug fix template has no name (not an issue when we weren't previously displaying it in a select menu); I pushed a commit to give it a name.

I had also noticed that, and was going to point it out, but then I think it slipped my mind :sweat_smile:

> But if we wanted to match what dotcom is doing, then .github/{ISSUE,PULL_REQUEST}_TEMPLATE.md files (i.e. templates that aren't grouped under a directory) should never show up in a picker, but should get used either A) by default (if there was no picker), or B) when the user has chosen "blank" from the picker.

Right. Seems the right way to go.  
We can do this. Shall I do it in this PR itself?
Yes, please amend this PR! Thank you

@AliabbasMerchant Thanks for the updates! Note for the future: it's easier for us to go through review cycles if you refrain from force-pushing the branch. In general, we avoid force-pushing while multiple people are either working on or reviewing a branch. After a force-push, it's hard for us to tell exactly which code is new since last review.

When the PR is approved to merge, we can always clean up the history by doing a rebase before the big merge.

@mislav Right, sorry. I won't force push from now on. Will clean up the history only after the PR is approved.  
For now, only the last 2 commits have changed contents.

In accordance with @mislav 's suggestion, the new workflow is as follows:  
Templates are now categorised into 2: 
1. LegacyTemplates: The `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md' and `ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md` files. Only 1 such template is respected, in order of occurrence in the '.github', root and 'docs' folder.
2. NonLegacyTemplates: The custom/special/non-generic templates in the `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE` and `ISSUE_TEMPLATE` folders

When the NonLegacyTemplates are present, the user is given a prompt to choose from them and a blank template(which defaults to the LegacyTemplate, if it is there, or an empty body)
If there are no NonLegacy templates, the legacy template is selected by default, if present, otherwise an empty body is selected.

There are currently no tests for template selection, but @vilmibm and I working on them in #986
@mislav Did you get the chance to test this out?
I have tried this out and it works great for me! Thank you
@AliabbasMerchant @safv12 Each `*_TEMPLATE` value is only repeated twice, so for now I'm making a call that it's fine. Thank you!

issue_context.title: Allow choosing a blank issue/pr template
issue_context.body:
> My expectation (just as the UI does), is to see the list of templates in any case (even if we have only one) because we should have something like `Blank` available to get a clean issue without any template.

_Originally posted by @gianarb in https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/503#issuecomment-588236044_
comments: I'm in favor of this! We could borrow the `Open a blank issue` language from github.com?

@ampinsk Generally I'm in favor of matching GitHub.com copy, but in this case as a user I might be confused thinking that "blank issue" means that the issue will be immediately submitted without body and that I won't get a chance to edit the issue. Maybe we could use language like “Skip template” or something similar?
That's a really good point. How about `No template`?

So should we go ahead with "No template"?  
I would like to implement this as a PR, if its okay.
Clicking on "Open a blank issue." in GitHub.com currently uses the template from `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md`, would this do that or would it just show a blank textbox?

@jack1142 Oh, I didn't know that GitHub.com did that, thanks!

@ampinsk What do you think the flow and copy should be if we followed what GitHub web UI does?
Ah thanks for clarifying @jack1142. It should match the GitHub.com behavior. So let’s go with “Open a blank issue” for the prompt, and use the “blank” template.

review_comments:
GitHub refers to the original way of `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` and `ISSUE_TEMPLATE.md` files as 'legacy' and the new method of `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE` and `ISSUE_TEMPLATE` folders containing the template files as "upgraded multiple template builder".  
I have hence called them as legacy and nonlegacy
How come you were able to remove `DeepEqual` comparison from here?
Coz `tt.want` is just a string now, since we only have at most a since legacy template file

I feel that the name of this struct should be changed, since it is not only used for issues, but for PRs also.  
Possibly to `metadataState`? :thinking:

In github-y terms, PRs _are_ issues since they are a subset of Issues. If we renamed this to `metadataState` in the `command` package then it might not be clear what the "metadata" applies to. I think the only more precise name would be "issueOrPullRequestMetadataState`

> In github-y terms, PRs are issues since they are a subset of Issues

Oh. I didn't know that.

> I think the only more precise name would be "issueOrPullRequestMetadataState`

Agreed. Can we do that, just for extra clarity?
I noticed that `"ISSUE_TEMPLATE"` string is used in multiple parts of the code. Could it be added to a constant?
The /choose route is to be opened only if we have non-legacy templates. If there is a legacy template only, it is selected by default by GitHub
